text: As the Patriots prepare to head to Jacksonville for a Week 3 AFC matchup with the Jaguars—who are looking to bounce back after their worst offensive performance in 11 months and banking on the Patriots being a team still "finding ourselves"—New England faces some significant roster complications heading into Sunday's 1 PM ET kickoff. The injury front looks particularly grim: starting right guard Mike Onwenu has a broken right ankle, rookie tight end Eli Raridon has returned to practice but remains uncertain for the contest, and safety Dell Pettus has been placed on injured reserve, prompting the Patriots to sign linebacker Jose Ramirez to the 53-man roster from the practice squad while adding linebacker Benton Whitley to the practice squad. Defensively, expect Jacksonville to lean heavily on Cover-6 coverage schemes, which will directly influence how the Patriots construct their gameplan around their bread-and-butter "X" plays, while on the other side of the ball, New England must dramatically improve its clock management before halftime after two consecutive games featured questionable decisions late in the second quarter. Through two weeks TreVeyon Henderson has found the end zone, and the defense showed its mettle in a 20-3 win over Pittsburgh, but the overall offensive rhythm remains elusive as the Patriots look to tighten things up in Florida.
